The accompanying tests show hoisting of inaccessible-memory calls and non-hoisting when another call reads the same inaccessible memory, indicating a refinement in MemorySSA-based alias/conflict reasoning.

Behavioral change: Adds a dominance-based filter in LICM's MemorySSA conflict scan: dominated accesses are ignored for non-sink cases.; Refines the invariant for hoisting by distinguishing inaccessible-memory calls that do or do not conflict with other accesses.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; removeFromLookups; memory access; still has uses
Reproducer link: Issue is an -O3 crash while updating MemorySSA; This commit changes LICM behavior around MemorySSA access scanning and hoisting decisions
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; Scalar transforms; MemorySSA

While the visible hunk does not mention removeFromLookups or the exact assertion, it does alter how MemorySSA accesses are considered during loop transformations, which is plausibly related to the reported crash class involving stale or conflicting memory-access bookkeeping.
